module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# $a(n) = (\text{smallest prime} > n^2) - n^2$

The difference between the smallest prime strictly greater than $n^2$ and $n^2$.

*References:*
- [A053000](https://oeis.org/A053000)-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA53000

/-- $a(n) = (\text{smallest prime} > n^2) - n^2$. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (sInf {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ n ^ 2 < p}) - n ^ 2

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 2 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 2 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := tsub_eq_of_eq_add <| IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) \le 1 + \phi(n)$ for $n > 0$. This improves on Oppermann's conjecture, which says
$a(n) < n$.
- Thomas Ordowski, Dec 17 2014
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : a n ≤ 1 + n.totient := by
  sorry

end OeisA53000

findings.description: The docstring credits the conjecture to "- Thomas Ordowski, Dec 17 2014". The OEIS entry credits this exact comment to Jianglin Luo, Sep 22 2023; the docstring copies the comment's text word for word. No Ordowski comment has ever been in A053000: archived snapshots from Apr 2015 (after the claimed Dec 2014 date) and Jan 2022 contain only the Legendre comment and M. F. Hasler's comment. None of the cross-referenced sequences I checked (A007491, A013632, A053001, A014085, A070316, A070317, A085099, A058055, A069003) mentions Ordowski either. The Lean statement `∀ n, 0 < n → a n ≤ 1 + n.totient` matches the comment exactly, so only the attribution is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A053000, %C line: "Conjecture: a(n) <= 1+phi(n) = 1+A000010(n), for n>0. This improves on Oppermann's conjecture, which says a(n) < n. - _Jianglin Luo_, Sep 22 2023". Sources: oeisdata seq/A053/A053000.seq, revision #56 of Jul 02 2025 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A053/A053000.seq), and the Wayback snapshot of https://oeis.org/A053000 dated 2025-11-19. The snapshots dated 2015-04-04 and 2022-01-03 have no Ordowski comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attribution line "- Thomas Ordowski, Dec 17 2014" with "- Jianglin Luo, Sep 22 2023".

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A007/A007491.seq (and A013632, A053001, A014085, A070316, A070317, A085099, A058055, A069003, A000010 from the same mirror, grepped for Ordowski/phi/Oppermann)
review.notes:
What I checked for each declaration:
- `OeisA53000.a`: `sInf {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ n^2 < p} - n^2`. I proved in a scratch file that the set is always nonempty (so the `sInf ∅ = 0` default is never reached), that n^2 + a n is prime with a n > 0, and that no prime lies strictly between n^2 and n^2 + a n. So `a` is exactly (smallest prime > n^2) - n^2, and the truncated subtraction never truncates. a 0 = 2 matches OEIS offset 0.
- The tests `a_0`–`a_4` give (2, 1, 1, 2, 1), which matches the OEIS data. I recomputed a(n) independently for n ≤ 10000 and it agrees with T. D. Noe's b-file everywhere.
- `conjecture`: `0 < n → a n ≤ 1 + n.totient` is the OEIS comment "a(n) <= 1+phi(n) = 1+A000010(n), for n>0"; `Nat.totient` is Euler's phi with φ(1) = 1.
- Boundary cases: the bound fails at n = 0 (a 0 = 2 > 1 = 1 + φ 0), so the hypothesis is needed. With a C program I found no violation for 1 ≤ n ≤ 3·10^6. Equality holds at n = 12, 18, 42 (e.g. a 12 = 5 = 1 + φ 12, confirmed in Lean), so a strict `<` would be false and `≤` is right.
- Difficulty: since 1 + φ(n) ≤ 1 + n < 2n + 1, the statement implies Legendre's conjecture, so it cannot be proved trivially.
- Status: `research open` is correct. Ferreira's unrefereed preprint (arXiv 2307.08725) claims results only for sufficiently large numbers, which cannot settle a statement about all n > 0.
- The "Oppermann says a(n) < n" remark in the docstring is copied from OEIS. It is really only for n > 1, but it is not formalized, so it has no effect on the Lean.

Access note: oeis.org's HTML entry pages were behind a Cloudflare challenge, so I read the entry text from the OEIS Foundation's oeisdata mirror. A Wayback snapshot of the live page from 2025-11-19 matches it.
